default: Use sentence case for headings, buttons, labels — capitalize only the first word and proper nouns. Never use English Title Case (Capitalizing Every Word).
Use formal/polite second-person register consistently across the UI (German Sie, French vous, Spanish usted, Russian вы, Polish Pan/Pani context, Arabic formal). Avoid the informal du/tu/tú/ты/ty.
Translate UI verbs as imperative or short button form, idiomatic to the target language (e.g. 'Save' → DE 'Speichern', FR 'Enregistrer', ES 'Guardar', IT 'Salva').
Progress states (Saving…, Loading…, Creating account…) translate to natural progressive forms in the target language.
Technical English terms STAY in English in the same letter case as source: webhook, Bearer, HMAC, token, API, OAuth, SDK, intranet, CRM. Do not translate them.
Brand and product names (Lisent, Tolgee, Meta, WhatsApp, SuperTokens, Nango, Dokploy, GreenAPI) are NEVER translated, NEVER inflected.
German specifics: nouns are always capitalized (Konto, Workspace, Kunde) — this is German grammar, not Title Case. Verbs and adjectives use sentence case.
Arabic: keep brand names in Latin script unless an established Arabic transliteration exists. Maintain right-to-left punctuation conventions where applicable.
Pluralization with {count}: use the target language's natural counter convention. After Turkish/Hungarian-style numerals the noun stays singular; in most European languages plural is normal.
tr: Use Turkish SENTENCE CASE for headings, titles, button labels, error messages: only the first letter of the first word is capitalized; everything else lowercase except proper nouns and brand names. NEVER use English Title Case (Capitalizing Every Word Like This). Example: 'Create your workspace access' → 'Çalışma alanı erişiminizi oluşturun' (NOT 'Çalışma Alanı Erişiminizi Oluşturun').

Use formal second-person plural 'siz' / possessive '-iniz' / verb suffixes '-iniz' consistently across ALL user-facing copy. Never use informal 'sen' / '-in'. Example: 'Already have access?' → 'Zaten erişiminiz var mı?'. 'Enter your password' → 'Parolanızı girin'. 'Capture core contact details' → 'Temel iletişim bilgilerini girin' (NOT 'yakala'/'yakalayın' — too literal; use 'girin' or 'kaydedin').
Translate UI button verbs as imperative second-person plural: 'Save' → 'Kaydet' (button label, idiomatic short form), 'Enter your password' → 'Parolanızı girin' (instruction).
Progress states (-ing, …) use Turkish present-continuous-passive: 'Saving...' → 'Kaydediliyor...', 'Creating account...' → 'Hesap oluşturuluyor...', 'Loading...' → 'Yükleniyor...'.
Use em dash — for English em dashes, en dash – for ranges. Avoid hyphen - as a sentence-level dash.

Technical English terms (webhook, intranet, Bearer, HMAC, token, CRM, API, OAuth, SDK) STAY in English in the same letter case as the source. Do NOT translate them to Turkish ('iç ağ', 'web kancası', 'taşıyıcı', 'belirteç' are WRONG). Example: 'Bearer' → 'Bearer'. 'web kancası' is unacceptable — use 'webhook'.
Possessive constructions: prefer Turkish genitive form. Example: 'Lisent's settings' → 'Lisent ayarları' (NOT 'Lisent'in ayarları' unless the brand truly takes a possessive marker).

Pluralization: do NOT add Turkish plural suffix '-lar/-ler' when source is already plural via context (e.g. {count} ahead). 'permanently delete {count} leads' → 'Bu, {count} müşteri adayını kalıcı olarak siler' (singular noun after counter — Turkish convention).
